## Proposed Teaching Plan {#teaching-plan}

- Teaching-week numbers below exclude Spring Break.
- The dated schedule above counts calendar weeks, including the break.
- This sequence is proposed; assessment dates have not been assigned.

<details>
<summary><strong>Fifteen teaching weeks</strong></summary>

| Teaching week | Proposed focus |
|---:|:---|
| 1 | Why Bayesian?; begin Foundations |
| 2 | Finish Foundations: posterior inference, prediction, and interpretation |
| 3 | Proportions: priors, conjugacy, and posterior prediction |
| 4 | Finish Proportions; begin Means and Normal Models |
| 5 | Means, unknown variance, joint and marginal inference |
| 6 | Finish normal models and approximations; begin Linear Models |
| 7–8 | Linear Models: regression, matrix formulation, checking, and regularization |
| 9 | Finish Linear Models; begin GLMs and Hierarchies |
| 10–11 | GLMs, partial pooling, hyperpriors, and multilevel prediction |
| 12–13 | Posterior Computation: Monte Carlo, MCMC, samplers, and diagnostics |
| 14 | Finish computation; begin Model Choice |
| 15 | Model comparison, selected extensions, and integrative model critique |

</details>

## Content and Hour Budgets {#hour-budgets}

- **Units:** 60-minute hours.
- **Available time:** fifteen teaching weeks with two 75-minute meetings per week provide **37½ contact hours**.
- **Sketch:** a 40-hour planning sketch of possible content.
- **Plan:** fits the meeting pattern by trimming half an hour each from approximation detail and advanced computation, and 1½ hours from optional extensions.
- **Included:** worked examples, discussion, and synthesis.
- **Further adjustment:** examinations or project presentations held in regular class time reduce the content budget.
